system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — CYS Investments, Inc. realized record after merger into Two Harbors Investment Corp., ~3-5-year horizon (~2021-2023)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because CYS Investments, Inc. was merged into a
> subsidiary of Two Harbors Investment Corp. and its securities removed from listing,
> there is no separate post-closing public 10-K for CYS; the traceable realized record
> is limited to CYS's own final disclosures and Two Harbors' subsequent annual reports.
> This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- CYS's own last EDGAR filing is the Current Report on Form 8-K reporting completion of
  the Merger, dated July 31, 2018; no subsequent periodic report (10-K, 10-Q) was filed
  by CYS. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-232852, Form 8-K]
- The NYSE filed Form 25/25-NSE notifications on 2018-08-01 removing CYS common stock,
  Series A preferred stock, and Series B preferred stock from listing. [SRC:
  https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001396446&type=25&owner=include&count=40]
- A search of EDGAR for Form 15 (types 15, 15-12B, 15-12G, 15-15D) under CYS's CIK
  (0001396446) returns no filings, notwithstanding CYS's stated intent in its closing
  8-K to file one; no further CYS-filed disclosure of any kind exists after July 31,
  2018. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001396446&type=15&owner=include&count=40]
- No separate audited financial statements or business-line disclosure specific to the
  acquired CYS asset portfolio were located in Two Harbors' subsequent annual reports
  for fiscal years 2021 or 2022 (the two 10-Ks falling within the ~2021-2023 outcome
  window); each 10-K's exhibit index references the CYS Merger Agreement only as a
  historical exhibit, with no narrative discussion of CYS as a distinct business
  segment. [SRC: SEC accession 0001465740-22-000018, Form 10-K (FY2021); SRC: SEC
  accession 0001465740-23-000055, Form 10-K (FY2022)]

## Realized record traceable to the surviving parent (Two Harbors) disclosures
- Two of CYS's former independent directors who were appointed to the Two Harbors board
  at closing, Karen Hammond and James A. Stern, are listed as sitting Two Harbors
  directors on the signature pages of Two Harbors' Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021
  (signed February 28, 2022) and fiscal year 2022 (signed February 28, 2023) — i.e.,
  approximately 3.5 and 4.5 years after the July 31, 2018 closing, respectively. [SRC:
  SEC accession 0001465740-22-000018, Form 10-K (FY2021); SRC: SEC accession
  0001465740-23-000055, Form 10-K (FY2022)]
- Two Harbors continued to be audited by Ernst & Young LLP and continued to be
  externally managed, with no disclosed change in its Agency RMBS / non-Agency / MSR
  business description in either the FY2021 or FY2022 Form 10-K. [SRC: SEC accession
  0001465740-22-000018, Form 10-K (FY2021); SRC: SEC accession 0001465740-23-000055,
  Form 10-K (FY2022)]

## Items sought but not found
- No source was located in which Two Harbors separately discloses a financial scalar
  (net income/loss, impairment, write-down, divestiture, or asset-retention statement)
  attributable specifically to the acquired CYS asset portfolio, as distinct from Two
  Harbors' consolidated results, within the ~2021-2023 outcome window. Per the no-record
  convention, no consolidated-company scalar is cited here as a CYS-specific outcome
  fact. [UNVERIFIED]
- No reputable-press report was located describing a documented divestiture, wind-down,
  or reversal specific to the former CYS asset portfolio within the outcome window.
  [UNVERIFIED]
- Whether any of CYS's four former named executive officers (Grant, DeCicco, Cleary,
  Rosenbloom) received severance under their employment agreements, or what became of
  them after ceasing to be CYS officers at closing, could not be sourced from any
  filing located within the outcome window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because CYS Investments, Inc. was merged into a subsidiary of Two Harbors Investment
  Corp. on July 31, 2018 and its securities were removed from NYSE listing, with no
  Form 15 or subsequent periodic report ever filed under CYS's own CIK, there is no
  separate public audited outcome record for CYS as a distinct business for the
  ~2021-2023 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-232852, Form 8-K; SRC:
  https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001396446&type=15&owner=include&count=40]
- The only traceable post-close realized-record facts are that two former CYS
  independent directors remained on the surviving parent's (Two Harbors') board through
  at least the FY2022 Form 10-K, and that the parent continued operating under the same
  externally managed Agency-RMBS business description with no disclosed CYS-specific
  segment. [SRC: SEC accession 0001465740-22-000018, Form 10-K (FY2021); SRC: SEC
  accession 0001465740-23-000055, Form 10-K (FY2022)]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the outcome for the
  acquired business: the absence of any separate CYS-specific public disclosure by the
  acquirer precludes a sourced determination of the realized 3-5-year trajectory of the
  specific acquired asset base.

[SLICE END]

No evidence bears on the archetype or business-model reconciliation, so t1 and t2 are uncertain.'}, name='emit_outcome_coding', type='tool_use')]
